differences.title: 1. TRANSPORT LAYER
differences.leftDesc: Leverages QUIC (built on UDP) for multiplexing, reduced head-of-line blocking, and faster connection establishment by avoiding TCP's three-way handshake.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on TCP, which can suffer from head-of-line blocking across different connections and requires a handshake, potentially leading to higher latency.

differences.title: 2. STREAMING MODES
differences.leftDesc: Supports both unreliable (datagrams) and reliable (streams) communication, with unidirectional streams minimizing head-of-line blocking even within a single connection.
differences.rightDesc: Primarily offers bidirectional streams, meaning both client and server can send data simultaneously on the same stream, but subject to TCP's blocking.

differences.title: 3. HEAD-OF-LINE BLOCKING
differences.leftDesc: QUIC's stream multiplexing on UDP prevents packet loss in one stream from blocking others, drastically improving performance for interactive apps.
differences.rightDesc: TCP's HOL blocking means a lost packet on a single connection halts all data transfer on that connection until it's retransmitted.

differences.title: 4. CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT
differences.leftDesc: QUIC allows for 0-RTT or 1-RTT connection setup, reducing latency for subsequent connections by sending data with the initial handshake.
differences.rightDesc: WebSockets over TLS typically requires a TCP handshake (1-RTT) plus a TLS handshake (1-RTT), leading to higher initial latency.

differences.title: 5. RELIABILITY CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: Offers independent reliability guarantees per stream, allowing mixing of reliable and unreliable data flows without impacting each other's guarantees.
differences.rightDesc: Reliability is managed at the connection level, meaning all data shares the same retransmission and ordering policies defined by TCP.

differences.title: 6. BANDWIDTH ESTIMATION
differences.leftDesc: QUIC has advanced, built-in congestion control and bandwidth estimation algorithms that adapt more dynamically to network conditions than traditional TCP.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on the underlying TCP stack's congestion control mechanisms, which can be less sophisticated and slower to adapt to changing network environments.

differences.title: 7. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for demanding real-time applications like multiplayer games, live video/audio streaming, and collaborative editing where low latency is critical.
differences.rightDesc: Suitable for general-purpose real-time communication, such as live notifications, basic chat applications, and status updates where latency is less critical.
